question.text: Under Ch 12, the 'Indenture of Trust' is relevant to institutional investor DD PRIMARILY because:

answer.text: It sets the Manager's performance fee.
It determines the fund's hurdle rate and clawback terms.
It specifies the exit strategy and IPO preferences.
It determines the nature of trust (Determinate vs Indeterminate) and the applicable tax rates — impacting beneficial ownership and whether tax is paid by the fund or by investors.

explanation.text: The Logic: Ch 12: Indenture of Trust is an 'important document to determine the tax liability of institutional investors and the beneficial ownership in the Trust structure'. Determinate vs Indeterminate status drives Income-tax treatment. The Trap: A, B, C all relate to PPM/Contribution Agreement, not the Trust Deed. Cross-Exam Context: Determinate/Indeterminate trust concept appears in tax modules of IA L2 (X-B) and RA (XV) for client tax-planning questions. Manager's Pro-Tip: Always get a tax-counsel opinion on trust determinacy filed in the data room. Foreign LPs' tax teams will ask — and will walk if they get uncertainty.
